messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] residual image
parts:
I don't have access to this file, so can't comment on it in particular,
but in general:
> All 24 of my chips have the same pattern -- the diagonal pink squares.

I have seen this type of spatial pattern on exon arrays before (if that is
indeed the type of data you're looking at). My guess is these are some
kind of special probes (genomic controls and so on) which do not form part
of a gene and so are not fitted (and hence have zero residuals).

Cheers,

Ken

messages.author: 0e065001d5e74ca3
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: residual image
parts: > Would the controls usually have such a patterned location on the chips?

It's quite possible, especially if they are alignment features (the
"landing lights" Affy uses to align the grid during image analysis).

> Also, would the same thing happen for the probe/probesets that are in
> the full annotation but not in the core cdf file (if your analysis is
> using the ,core.cdf file)? Can you choose what color these types of
> things are (e.g. grey or white)?

Yes, any probes not in the core cdf will have zero residuals. I guess you
might be able to specify a colour for these, but you'd need to know the
cell locations.

Ken
